excerpt: Workstream is HR, hiring and payroll software for businesses with hourly workers, such as restaurants and retail. What it does, plans and alternatives.
content:
Workstream is a San Francisco company that makes HR and payroll software for businesses that employ hourly workers, with a strong focus on restaurants, retail and healthcare. It started as a text-based hiring tool: TechCrunch reported in 2021 that Workstream had been working on recruitment for hourly workers since 2017, letting candidates apply and schedule interviews by text. Its website now covers the wider employee life cycle: applicant tracking and AI voice and video screening, mobile onboarding with documents and I-9/E-Verify, team chat, time clocks and shift scheduling, full-service payroll, benefits administration and labour-law compliance alerts.

Desmond Lim is Workstream's co-founder and CEO. TechCrunch reported that, at the time of its 2021 raise, Workstream had 1,500 customers across about 10,000 stores, naming McDonald's, Subway and Jamba Juice among them.

Funding

In August 2021 Workstream raised a $48 million Series B co-led by BOND and Coatue, with Zoom's Eric Yuan and DoorDash's Tony Xu among the backers; its earlier $10 million Series A was led by Founders Fund. In September 2022 the company announced a further $60 million, led by GGV Capital, which took the Series B to $108 million.

Pricing

Workstream's pricing page lists four tiers, Hiring, Essentials, All-in-one and Premium, each including the one before, plus add-ons for time and scheduling, ACA and benefits, and compliance. No prices are shown; every tier asks you to get in touch for a quote.

We have not used Workstream. This page is based on Workstream's website and pricing page (checked 15 October 2026), TechCrunch's 2021 report and the company's 2022 funding announcement.
